title: Security & Compliance Control Playbook: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence & Exceptions
author: Priya Kapoor
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates Redwood Inference's operational controls and procedures for role-based access control (RBAC) and authentication, audit logging, data residency and retention, secure SDLC gates, incident-response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and the risk/exception lifecycle. It is intended for engineers, product owners, and auditors.

Scope: Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and to all Redwood-managed control planes, data stores, and CI/CD pipelines.

Owners and contacts
- Primary owner: Security Team (security@redwood-inference.com)
- Secondary owners: Eng Platform (eng-platform@redwood-inference.com), Eng Infra (eng-infra@redwood-inference.com)
- On-call: sec-oncall rotation (PagerDuty service: RED_SEC_ONCALL)

1) RBAC and Authentication

Summary: RBAC is enforced at three layers: cloud IAM (GCP/AWS), internal service-level ACLs (auth-service), and application feature flags. We follow least privilege, JIT provisioning, and periodic access reviews.

Roles (canonical):
- org-admin: company SRE/Platform leads. Full org-level cloud permissions; used sparingly.
- sec-admin: security engineers with access to audit logs, key management, and incident tooling.
- infra-engineer: cluster/network operations.
- platform-engineer: runtime and model-serving owners.
- developer: standard write access to non-prod and repository-level rights as scoped.
- read-only-auditor: read-only access to logs, metrics, and config for auditors/compliance.
- service-account: machine identity; no human login.

Enforcement details:
- SSO: Okta is the authoritative IdP. All human users must authenticate via Okta SSO with enforced MFA (TOTP + hardware keys allowed).
- SCIM: User and group provisioning is automated via SCIM from Okta into cloud IAM and internal auth-service.
- Short-lived credentials: Service accounts issued short-lived tokens (max 6h) via our token broker (auth-broker). Long-lived keys are not permitted without explicit exception.
- Role binding policy: All role bindings must be requested via the Access Request Jira project (ACCESS) with an approver from the owner team. Access is auto-expired after 90 days unless renewed.

Sample internal policy (auth-service) - JSON example:
{
  "principal": "group:platform-engineers@redwood-inference.com",
  "resource": "/models/*/deploy",
  "effect": "allow",
  "actions": ["deploy", "update"]
}

Periodic reviews:
- Quarterly automated access reviews triggered for all org-admin and sec-admin roles.
- Annual company-wide access certification for auditors and compliance.

2) Audit Logging and Log Integrity

Goal: Centralize immutable audit logs for authentication, authorization decisions, configuration changes, and production data access. Ensure tamper-evidence and availability for forensic investigations.

Architecture and flows:
- Sources: auth-service, api-gateway, runtime-proxy, model-serving-control-plane, billing, and deployment pipelines emit structured audit events to the audit-ingest pipeline.
- Collector: audit-logger (Kafka topic: audit.events) -> processing -> write to Cloud Logging (GCP) or CloudWatch Logs + S3 (AWS), and a hardened append-only store (WORM-backed S3 bucket: s3://redwood-audit-worm).
- Indexing: Events are indexed into the audit index in Elasticsearch/Opensearch for fast queries (retained per retention policy).

SLOs / thresholds:
- Audit event delivery: 99.9% of events delivered to primary store within 60s.
- Search query latency (90p): < 2s for 30d window.

Retention and integrity controls:
- Retention: See 'Data residency & retention' section for retention periods. Audit events classified as security-critical are stored in WORM for 7 years by default.
- Integrity: All audit payloads are hashed and signed using KMS key ring 'audit-signing-key' (KMS ID: projects/redwood/kms/keyRings/audit/cryptoKeys/sign). Signatures are stored with the event record.
- Access: Only sec-admin and read-only-auditor roles can retrieve raw audit WORM objects. Retrieval is logged and must be justified in ACCESS ticket.

Common CLI examples:
- GCP (Cloud Logging):
  gcloud logging read 'resource.type="project" AND logName="projects/redwood/logs/audit"' --limit=50 --format=json
- AWS (CloudTrail lookup):
  aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=AssumeRole --max-results 50

Sample audit event (JSON):
{
  "ts": "2026-02-28T15:12:01Z",
  "actor": "user:alice@redwood-inference.com",
  "action": "models.deploy",
  "resource": "/models/llama-2:v1/deployments/d1",
  "outcome": "success",
  "signature": "MEUCIQDx...",
  "hash": "sha256:abcd1234..."
}

3) Data Residency and Retention

Classification and residency rules:
- Data classes: public, internal, customer_data, pii, phi.
- Residency zones: US (us-central1 / us-east-1), EU (europe-west1 / eu-west-1), APAC (ap-southeast-1) – customer contracts may require strict regional isolation.

Retention matrix (examples):
- pii: retention = 7 years; storage location = customer-designated region; deletion: manual plus automated scrub; backup retention = 90 days
- customer_data (non-PII): retention = 2 years; deletion on request within 30 days
- audit events (security-critical): retention = 7 years in WORM store
- logs (infra): retention = 90 days in hot index, 3 years in cold archive

Implementation examples:
- S3 lifecycle (example policy):
  {
    "Rules": [
      {
        "ID": "pii-worm",
        "Filter": {"Prefix": "pii/"},
        "Status": "Enabled",
        "NoncurrentVersionExpiration": {"NoncurrentDays": 3650}
      }
    ]
  }
- BigQuery dataset policy: datasets are created with location=EU for EU-resident datasets and with table-level expiration set per retention matrix.

Data deletion and subject access requests (SARs):
1. SAR is submitted to privacy@redwood-inference.com or via the customer portal.
2. Privacy team opens ticket in PRIVACY project and verifies identity.
3. Engineering owner runs deletion playbook (script below) and logs artifact.

Deletion script (example):
  # run as infra-engineer with ACCESS ticket id
  aws s3 rm s3://customer-bucket/path/to/customerid --recursive --region eu-west-1
  bq query --use_legacy_sql=false 'DELETE FROM `redwood_eu.dataset.table` WHERE customer_id="CUST-12345"'

4) Secure SDLC Controls

Gates and tooling:
- Repositories: All code stored in GitHub Enterprise. Branch protection: require 2 approvers for prod-facing repos, mandatory linear history, and required status checks.
- CI/CD: GitHub Actions + self-hosted runners in private subnets. Builds must pass: unit tests, integration smoke tests, Snyk scan (vuln threshold set to fail on critical), and secret-scan.
- Artifact signing: Release artifacts are signed with the build pipeline key (KMS key: build-signing) and checksummed. Artifact manifests include provenance metadata.
- Dependency policy: Dependabot enabled; critical/important CVEs require remediation within 7 days.

Pre-deploy checklist (example):
1. All tests passed and coverage >= 85% (for critical services).
2. No critical Snyk or OSS critical vulnerabilities.
3. Performance regression check against canary baseline.
4. Rollout policy defined (canary %s, failover).

Example GitHub Action snippet (required status check):
name: "CI - gating"
on: [push]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: self-hosted
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Run unit tests
        run: make test
      - name: Snyk scan
        run: snyk test || exit 1

5) Incident Response – Security Procedures

Severity levels (brief):
- Sev1 (Critical): Active compromise, data exfiltration confirmed, production-wide impact. Response time: immediate; sec-oncall page + exec comms.
- Sev2 (High): Targeted compromise or service degradation with potential data exposure. Response time: 1 hour.
- Sev3 (Medium): Isolated misconfiguration or non-sensitive data exposure. Response time: 4 hours.

Triage and containment runbook (high-level):
1. Triage: Sec-oncall and oncall-sre join incident channel (Slack #incidents). Record initial timeline and suspected blast radius.
2. Evidence preservation: Snapshot affected VMs, preserve disk images, export relevant audit logs, and disable any log rotation that would purge events.
3. Containment: Rotate service credentials, revoke compromised sessions, apply temporary ACLs (auth-service:deny for affected principals).
  - CLI example to revoke tokens (auth-broker):
    curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
      https://auth-broker.redwood-inference.internal/admin/revoke --data '{"principal":"service:uptstream-worker"}'
4. Forensics: Copy logs to forensics bucket and assign case owner. Engage external IR vendor if required.
5. Remediation: Patch vulnerabilities, restore from known-good artifacts, and perform a staged redeploy with canary monitoring.
6. Post-incident: Postmortem within 7 business days, include timeline, root cause analysis, and action items.

Key exec and communication steps:
- Exec notification threshold: any Sev1 incident must trigger the Exec Incident call within 2 hours.
- Customer notification: Follow the customer-notification policy in security-and-compliance/security-and-compliance-playbook; legal and CS must be looped for data-affecting incidents.

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Automated evidence collection:
- Evidence-runner service (internal) can collect: IAM role bindings, access request logs, build artifact manifests, Snyk scan results, test run artifacts, and audit-log extracts. Evidence bundles are compressed and signed, then uploaded to the compliance-evidence store (encrypted with key 'evidence-store-key').

Manual evidence process for auditors:
1. Auditor raises request via compliance@redwood-inference.com with scope and timeframe.
2. Compliance team creates evidence bundle using evidence-runner with the request ID.
3. Bundle stored in the secure evidence bucket and link shared with auditor.

Sample command to create evidence bundle:
  ./evidence-runner collect --scope=repo:runtime --since=2025-12-01 --ticket=AUD-4567 --output=aud-4567-bundle.tar.gz

Evidence retention and handling:
- Evidence bundles are retained for the duration of the audit + 3 years. Access to evidence bundles is audited and limited to compliance and sec-admin roles.

7) Risk & Exceptions Process

When a control cannot be met, teams must submit an exception request. Minimum required fields:
- service_name, control_id, risk_description, compensating_controls, requested_duration, owner, approver

Approval matrix:
- Low risk: Team lead + security reviewer (auto-approve window <= 30 days)
- Medium risk: Security manager + Platform engineering approver (<= 90 days)
- High risk: CISO + CTO approval (time-limited; <= 180 days)

Compensating controls examples:
- Increased monitoring (10s log polling), additional alerting, temporary network isolation, privileged session recording.

Tracking and expiry:
- Exceptions are tracked in Jira project RISK. Automatic reminders 14 days before expiry. Exceptions must include a mitigation plan and a sunset date.

Template exception request (Jira fields):
- Summary: "Exception: Allow long-lived key for data-migration (service: data-migrator)"
- Labels: exception, high-risk
- Fields: service_name="data-migrator"; control_id="RBAC-003"; requested_duration=180; compensating_controls="shortened key scope + session recording"

Appendix: Ownership, links & SLOs
- Audit delivery SLO: 99.9% delivered within 60s (owner: eng-platform).
- Access review cadence: Quarterly (owner: security).
- Artifact signing: All prod releases must be signed (owner: eng-developer-experience).
